thread:
maria: quick thing — we've been seeing churn in dedicated pools when customers send 10–30s spikes. churn = nodes added then immediately drained, KV cache misses, + latency. thinking we should split admission intent from scaling intent and add a short-lived ephemeral burst lane. any concerns?
kevin: sounds sensible. separating admission vs scale control loops tends to reduce oscillation. main worry is abuse: repeated micro-bursts could eat headroom. need a per-tenant token budget or rate-limiter for ephemeral lanes. :thinking_face:
ashok: +1. ephemeral nodes should have strict TTL and zero-cost fallback (lower-tier model) if budget exhausted. also consider prewarming tiny KV caches on ephemeral nodes (maybe snapshot from warm pool) to avoid full cold start penalty.
nate: idea for an "Intent" proto we could pass to autoscaler:```proto
message Intent {
  string tenant_id = 1;
  float qps_estimate = 2;    // requests per second
  int64 expected_ms = 3;     // expected duration ms
  int32 priority = 4;        // 0..10
  float token_weight = 5;    // weight for credit system
}
```Use TTL/hysteresis on intent lifetime: only escalate scale intent after repeated intents or sustained high qps.
julia: agree on credits. we should tie ephemeral budget to reserved capacity (dedicated contracts) so enterprise customers don't get surprised. safety cap per-pool: never exceed N% of pool for ephemeral nodes. also need metrics: ephemeral_count, ephemeral_eviction_rate, intent_rate_by_tenant.
kevin: operationally, I want two control loops: AdmissionController (fast, decides if we accept requests into burst lane) and ScalePlanner (slower, changes node counts). Admission returns client hints: ACCEPTED/BACKOFF/DEGRADED. Admission should be stateless-ish and use short-term counters from aggregator.
maria: how do we avoid gaming? tenant can just send tiny bursts repeatedly. propose exponential backoff per-tenant for ephemeral acceptance and decaying credit pool. documented enforcement policy in console.
ashok: for countermeasures: credit bucket with refill rate tied to purchased quota + small free tier. eviction policy: evict ephemeral nodes first; prefer to keep reserved tenants' cores.
ate: (typo) nate: also think about how rollout interacts with preemption: if pool gets tight, ephemeral gone first and we need quick fallback models. Add automatic fallback config per-tenant.
infra-bot: sim-run: autoscaler-sim v2 on testbed finished. result: with 3s intent hysteresis and per-tenant credit=5, oscillation reduced ~73%, 95p cold-start reduced 48%. logs: https://ci.redwood/sim/2293344556
kevin: nice. can we get sim to cover pathological pattern: 15s spike every 45s from 50 tenants? that's the one that currently kills us.
nate: I'll extend sim scenarios. Also will prototype intent proto + client header X-Redwood-Intent for SDKs.
julia: I'll draft dashboards and alert rules: spike-rate, ephemeral-utilization, intent-throttle-rate. want a runbook for when ephemeral exhaustion coincides with model fallback errors.
maria: next steps: open RFC PR with design, include sim results, add acceptance criteria (no >2x churn on synthetic workload). owners: kevin (admission prototype), nate (intent + SDK), ashok (warm snapshot design), julia (metrics), maria (RFC draft). ETA: spike plan by EOW?
kevin: EOW prototype ok.
ashok: will start snapshot sketch tomorrow.
